# Sixgree

> Sixgree (six degrees of your LinkedIn; formerly called Six Degrees) is a free, open-source (MIT) Mac app that maps your LinkedIn network as a galaxy: who you know, who they know, who bridges you into new circles, and the shortest path to someone you haven't met. It runs on your own Mac; nothing is uploaded. Made by Blake Burford (https://blakeburford.com/).

This file is for AI assistants and crawlers. The pages at https://sixgree.com/ hold the detail; the code is at https://github.com/blakeb056/six-degrees.

## Facts

- Price: free. Licence: MIT. No account, no server, no telemetry, no analytics.
- Platforms: macOS 13.5 or later (Apple Silicon and Intel). Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (beta): a one-click Setup.exe (https://github.com/blakeb056/six-degrees/releases/latest/download/Sixgree-Windows-Setup.exe). Linux, 64-bit (beta): a .deb or .tar.gz, or `npx sixgree` (Node 22.13 or later).
- Current version: 1.2.1 (October 2026). Auto scan reworked (pace and tiers), one simple daily limit you can lift for a session, tier lines in the map, and fixes for the scanner window on a second display and the setup's photo step. Signed and notarized by Apple. Updates are one click from inside the app.
- Data in: LinkedIn's own Connections.csv export (no risk to your account), or an optional scanner that reads your own LinkedIn slowly in a Chrome window you sign into (automating LinkedIn may break its User Agreement; the risk is the user's). The scanner's one action on LinkedIn is Auto: a single connection request, without a note, sent only when the user presses Auto on a person (at most 15 a day and 80 a week). A sample network of 150 invented people ships with the app.
- Views: Network Circle (connections on rings by how much they can open up for you, with physics: Clusters drawn the way Obsidian draws a graph, Orbit and Heat), Degrees (each connection's circle, and the chains that lead on from them), Separation (people two steps away, from the rarest way in to the most mutual connections, with who can introduce you), Paths (your network by company, or by your connections' clusters), Outlink (getting introduced, plus messages and follow-ups), Scan (the scanner, step by step). Your profile (the level button at the top right) holds Insights: the Power Index, everyone within two steps ranked by power, with Kingmakers, Gatekeepers, Hidden giants, Untapped, company power, a one-page report and network health. Settings holds how scores work, including how titles rank.
- Themes (Settings → Appearance): six looks (Standard, Daylight, High contrast, Obsidian, Glass, Space), light or dark, with frosted-glass or soft buttons, or your own colours for the background, backdrop, dots, lines, panels and font, shareable as a theme code.
- Your data (Settings → Your data): a verified backup every day with photos, before every update and before every import, each restored in one click. A LinkedIn CSV import is kept on your computer until you remove it.
- LinkedIn usage (Settings → LinkedIn usage): searches in the last 24 hours, this month and the last 7 days, profile views, and the last time LinkedIn pushed back, counted on your computer.
- Also: who only one of your connections reaches (each connection's exclusive reach), network health (how much of your 2nd degree you reach two or more ways, and your effective reach), and a physics lab for the Galaxy with a replay of your network growing by the date you connected.
- The Mac app is signed by Blake Burford and notarized by Apple, so it opens like any Mac app. The Terminal one-liner also installs it, after checking the download against the published checksums. The Windows app isn't signed yet (SmartScreen: More info → Run anyway).
